title: Two hundred thousand open flow mappings followed by 140,608 lines of distinct keys
notes: The input is never closed, so it is an error: a syntax error at the end of the input, or a limit error if the reader refuses the nesting first. No result is allowed. The keys of the innermost mapping are 140,608 different names (`xaaa` to `xZZZ`, none of them a number, boolean or null), so a reader that rejects duplicate keys still reads every line. This is the large form of safety/deep-flow-mappings-then-many-lines-unclosed, which has the same lines under 9,000 open mappings and sits in the fast set. A reader that looks at every open flow mapping for each line does about 28 billion steps here, and one that was measured does much more than that in proportion to the depth: it needed 3.9 seconds under 9,000 mappings and 233 seconds under 200,000. The time limit is 100 seconds and is a hang guard, not a measure of cost; the depth is chosen so that the reader measured above goes over it; a reader that does only the 28 billion steps may not, and readers that refuse the nesting at once, or read the lines in time proportional to their number, finish in a fraction of a second. The memory bound is the second check. The limits are the robustness requirement of the kit, not a rule of the specification. Input: 200,000 `{`, then each name followed by a comma and a line break; it is generated from the recipe in case.json (docs/case-format.md) and the case carries the tag `slow` because it is larger than a stored file.

provenance.reference: A reader whose time was quadratic here: each line was checked against the pending implicit-key slot of every open flow mapping, taking nine seconds for a five megabyte input of this shape.
